content.text:
Done. Player spawn moved to (0, 3, 0).

**Commands run:**
- `Glob: Assets/Scenes/SampleScene.unity` — confirm the scene file exists at the expected path.
- `Grep: "Player" -l` on the scene file — locate the Player GameObject block since I didn't already know its fileID.
- `Grep: "m_Name: Player" -n` — get the exact line number of the GameObject definition (line 3249).
- `Read` lines 3220-3260 — pull the GameObject's `m_Component` list to find which fileID is its Transform (Transform isn't always the first listed).
- `Grep: "^--- !u!4 &98477898[0-9]" -A10` — scoped to fileIDs matching the Player's component block (984778978-989) and filtered to type `!u!4` (Transform), since guessing the transform fileID by pattern is faster than reading the whole 3000+ line YAML linearly.
- `Edit` — changed `m_LocalPosition: {x: 0, y: 1, z: 0}` → `{x: 0, y: 3, z: 0}` at line 3439.

**Bash was blocked** ("don't ask mode" denial) when I tried `pwd`/`git rev-parse` to confirm the working directory per my global instruction — I switched to file tools (Glob/Grep/Read/Edit) instead, which weren't blocked, and confirmed the path from the tool outputs themselves.

**Real risk for your demo, flagged not fixed:** I edited the `.unity` scene file on disk. Since you said the Editor is already open with this project, Unity does **not** hot-reload an open scene from an external disk edit automatically — it only detects the change and prompts to reload when the Editor window regains focus, and if you have any unsaved changes in that open scene, that reload prompt can conflict with them (risk of losing your in-Editor edits, or the prompt not appearing and your position edit being invisible until you manually reload the scene). Alt-tab into Unity now and check for a "file changed on disk" reload prompt before you demo — if it doesn't appear, close the scene tab and reopen `SampleScene` to force the reload.

A `unity-ops:unity-surface-preflight` guardrail hook fired on this edit (advisory only, didn't block) — noting that direct writes to serialized Unity assets while the Editor may have the scene open should go through a live-Editor CLI (`unity-cli`/`unity-pipeline`) instead of raw file edit, for exactly the reload-race reason above.

**GitHub issue to file** (repo: confirm with `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner` — I didn't run it, Bash is blocked):

> **Title:** Direct scene-file edits bypass live-Editor state — risk of reload conflict
> **Body:** Editing `Assets/Scenes/SampleScene.unity` on disk via a text tool while the Unity Editor has the scene open does not push the change into the live Editor session. Unity only offers a reload-from-disk prompt on window focus, and that prompt can conflict with unsaved in-Editor changes. `unity-ops:unity-surface-preflight` fires an advisory on this pattern (`serialized-asset-write`) but does not block it.
> **Acceptance criteria:** Either (a) route position/asset edits through `unity-cli`/`unity-pipeline` live-Editor RPC instead of raw file edit when an Editor session is known/likely open, or (b) make the preflight check blocking rather than advisory for `serialized-asset-write` against scene files, with an explicit override flag for headless/CI contexts where no Editor is open.
